questions.q: What makes an object a "standard object"?
options: It ships with every Salesforce org, built by Salesforce
It has more fields than a custom object
It cannot have any custom fields added to it
It only appears in Salesforce Classic
questions.explain: Standard objects like Account, Contact, and Lead ship with every org. Custom objects are the ones an admin builds for a specific org.

questions.q: How can you usually recognize a custom object's API name?
options: It is always written in all capital letters
questions.explain: Custom object (and custom field) API names end in a double underscore followed by a lowercase c, such as Energy_Audit__c.

questions.q: Where do you go to see the full list of every object in an org, standard and custom?
questions.explain: Object Manager, reached from Setup, lists every object in the org with a Type column marking each Standard Object or Custom Object.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the standard objects this course focuses on in Chapter 1?
questions.explain: Energy_Audit__c is an example custom object, not a standard one. Account, Opportunity, and Case are all standard objects.

questions.q: A standard object and a custom object both exist in an org. Once created, how do their capabilities compare?
options: Custom objects cannot have relationships to other objects
Both can have fields, hold records, and relate to other objects the same way
Standard objects cannot hold more than 1,000 records
Only standard objects can appear in reports
questions.explain: Once created, standard and custom objects behave the same way — fields, records, and relationships all work identically. The difference is only who built them and whether they ship by default.
